description:
Filed s395 while working #314's residue.  Keyed by REFUSAL TEXT the audit split
this feature across three of #314's families; keyed by CAUSE it is one feature
and the largest remaining block by a wide margin.

MEASURED (companion suite, s395 tree):
  t/re/opt.t           639 rows, TRANSPILE-FAIL on ONE line 46:
                       `our \$TODO = \$::TODO;`
  t/op/const-optree.t  148 rows, TRANSPILE-FAIL on `for \%_ (@tests)` (line 412)
  t/op/lvref.t         199 rows, TRANSPILE-FAIL on `\state @a = [1..3]`
  t/op/decl-refs.t     402 rows, currently 42 -- the file IS the feature's
                       syntax test (mostly eval-string + warning-text rows, so
                       expect a lower yield here than the row count suggests)
Plus, in perl-tests/: substr.t (1 commented-out block), aassign.t (two blocks),
each.t (one block) -- see docs/not-supported.md "Ref aliasing".

THE ENTRY'S PREMISE WAS FALSE and is corrected in the same doc: refaliasing was
NOT removed in 5.40.  Probed on perl 5.40.3 -- all five shapes below work and
warn only `Aliasing via reference is experimental`.

THE SHAPES, with their live-perl answers (probed s395):
  \my $x = \$y;              $x=7  =>  $y is 7        (scalar alias)
  \my @b = \@a;              push @b,3 => @a has 3    (array alias)
  \my %g = \%h;              $g{j}=2  => %h has j     (hash alias)
  our \$T = \$::TODO;        $T="tv"  => $::TODO tv   (package cell alias)
  for \my %e (@list) {...}   each element aliased in turn
Also `\$x = \$y` without a declarator (plain refaliasing), and the `state`
spelling `\state @a = [1..3]` (op/lvref.t).

WHY IT MAY BE CHEAP HERE (size this first, do not assume): in PCL a scalar
variable IS a p-box, so an alias is "make the two names hold the SAME box
object" -- for a lexical, bind the let variable to the referent box; for a
package variable, store the referent box in the cell.  A container alias is the
same move with the vector / hash-table object.  That is assignment of an
existing object, not a new indirection layer, and it is exactly what
`p-ref-target` already hands back.

THE HARD PARTS to check before committing to it:
  * the LVALUE side: `\$x` in lvalue position has to be recognised by the
    expression machinery (PPI: Cast '\' + Symbol), and the declarator forms
    (`\my $x`, `our \$T`, `\state @a`) reach Parser2's declaration matchers,
    which today refuse them (the three #314 refusal texts).
  * VarAnnotator: an aliased scalar can never be unboxed/frozen -- a write
    through either name must be visible through the other, so the alias must
    force the boxed path for BOTH names.
  * the foreach form (`for \%_ (@list)`) needs the loop variable BOUND to each
    element's referent, which is the #267 splitter's territory.
  * `\$h{foo} = \$var` (an alias INTO a container slot) is a different move
    from a variable alias and may not be worth the first pass.

BAR: probe the five shapes plus their INVERSE (a plain `my $x = \$y` must stay
a reference, not an alias); corpus-diff; gate; full sweep (a runtime change);
re-run the four t/ files and splice their snapshot rows; and DELETE the
docs/not-supported.md "Ref aliasing" entry rather than rephrasing it.

=== DONE s396 (four commits: d0032e8, 84afe27, ebabc69, fbb47cd, 342d82c) ===

The ASSIGNMENT forms and the FOREACH forms all work, probed row-for-row
against perl 5.40.3.  ONE arm in p-setf's place dispatch does it: a \\-cast
lvalue REBINDS THE NAME'S STORAGE to the right-hand referent.  Guard:
Pl/t/refaliasing-01.t (32 rows).

THE ROW ESTIMATE IN THIS TASK WAS 46% WRONG.  re/opt.t (639 of the ~1400) had
exactly one refusal, so it was sized as reachable; with the refusal gone it
transpiles, runs, and dies on re::optimization -- perl's XS readout of its own
regex optimizer.  Registered XDIFF.  A "one refusal blocks N rows" estimate is
an upper bound until the file has RUN.

Delivered: op/const-optree.t 0 -> 86 (task #327, the foreach spelling),
op/for-many.t 0 -> 63 (task #329, n-at-a-time), op/aassign.t 169 -> 173,
op/substr.t reaches its last test instead of crashing.

RESIDUE, each with its own cause, all named in docs/not-supported.md:
  * `my \$x` in RVALUE position (op/decl-refs.t is mostly this);
  * the feature-gating diagnostics (135 rows of op/decl-refs.t) -- same family
    as the general warnings model, task #221;
  * `\\state @a = [1..3]` -- blocked by #314 family F-F, not by aliasing
    (op/lvref.t 201 rows);
  * read-only SCALARS -> task #330.
subject: refaliasing / declared_refs - ONE feature behind ~1400 rows of #314 residue (re/opt.t, op/const-optree.t, op/lvref.t, op/decl-refs.t)
